title: A factorization after etale surjective base change makes higher-image transitions monic
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, k:T→S a scheme morphism, G an etale Λ-module sheaf on T, q an integer, and φ:U→V a morphism of schemes over T. Suppose g:S′→S is etale and surjective and a cartesian square P→V, P→S′ over V→S and g is given. If the projection P→V factors through φ:U→V, then the canonical higher-image transition R^q(V→S)_*(G|V)→R^q(U→S)_*(G|U) is monic [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions, def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square, def-weil-surjective-morphism].

proof.text: Apply etale base change along g. The pasting identity for the canonical adjunction-unit base-change maps identifies the pullback of the transition, followed by the map from the given factorization, with the cartesian base-change isomorphism. Thus the pulled-back map is split monic; applying homology preserves the splitting.

The surjective inverse image is exact and faithful. It therefore reflects monomorphisms of sheaves. The coefficient inverse-composition and single-functor comparisons in higherDirectImageOverMap are isomorphisms, so composition with them preserves monicity.
